cards.d: If something is done on one’s behalf, it is done for that person by another.
cards.e: The original speaker was sick, so his son gave the speech on his behalf.
cards.ielts: Charities often campaign on behalf of people who cannot speak for themselves, such as refugees and the homeless.

cards.d: To flap means to move quickly up and down or from side to side.
cards.e: The tiny bird flapped its wings and ate from the flowers.
cards.ielts: Flags flapped in the wind as thousands of protesters marched through the capital demanding action on climate change.

cards.d: A glacier is a large piece of ice that moves very slowly.
cards.e: The North Pole is covered by a huge glacier.
cards.ielts: The photographs show how dramatically the glacier has shrunk over the past fifty years as a result of global warming.

cards.d: The globe refers to the Earth.
cards.e: Water covers most of the globe.
cards.ielts: Fast food chains have spread across the globe, changing eating habits in countries with very different culinary traditions.

cards.d: When something is horizontal, it is flat and level with the ground.
cards.e: The Russian flag has three horizontal stripes of white, blue, and red.
cards.ielts: In the line graph, the horizontal axis shows the years from 1990 to 2020, while the vertical axis shows the population.

cards.d: To hum means to make a low, continuous noise.
cards.e: The man hummed his favorite song.
cards.ielts: Residents near the new data centre complain that its cooling fans hum constantly, even late at night.

cards.d: An inventory is a supply of something.
cards.e: Gwen was checking the inventory to make sure we had what we needed.
cards.ielts: Large supermarkets use computer systems to track their inventory, so shelves are restocked before products run out.

cards.d: If a thought or feeling is inward, it is not expressed or shown to others.
cards.e: She had an inward feeling of guilt when she lied to her mother.
cards.ielts: Although she smiled throughout the interview, she felt an inward panic when the examiner asked her about economics.

cards.d: A loaf of bread is bread shaped and baked in one piece.
cards.e: Could you please buy a loaf of bread for sandwiches?
cards.ielts: The bar chart shows that the price of a loaf of bread doubled in the UK between 2000 and 2022.

cards.d: An oracle is a person who speaks with gods and gives advice about the future.
cards.e: The king went to the oracle to ask if going to war was a good idea.
cards.ielts: In ancient Greece, leaders consulted an oracle before making important decisions, whereas modern governments rely on economic forecasts.

cards.d: To orbit something means to move around it in a continuous, curving path.
cards.e: The moon orbits the Earth.
cards.ielts: Thousands of satellites now orbit the Earth, providing services such as navigation, weather forecasting and internet access.

cards.d: An overview is a general description of a situation.
cards.e: My brother gave me an overview of the important parts of the book.
cards.ielts: In Task 1, you should always include an overview that summarises the main trends shown in the graph.

cards.d: A preview is an opportunity to see something before it is available to the public.
cards.e: The band played us a preview of their new song.
cards.ielts: Some museums offer local residents a free preview of new exhibitions before they open to the general public.

cards.d: If something is previous, then it happened earlier in time or order.
cards.e: He turned back to the previous page to read the paragraph again.
cards.ielts: Unemployment fell to four percent in 2019, compared with six percent in the previous year.

cards.d: To provide something means to supply it.
cards.e: Each student was provided with a test and three sharp pencils.
cards.ielts: Governments should provide free public transport for students and elderly people to reduce traffic and pollution.

cards.d: To recur means to happen more than once.
cards.e: Burglaries seem to recur over and over in our neighborhood.
cards.ielts: Flooding has become a recurring problem in the region, so the authorities are building new barriers along the river.

cards.d: When something is relevant, it is important to a certain person or situation.
cards.e: The thirty-year-old book about politics is still relevant to our society today.
cards.ielts: Schools should teach skills that are relevant to the modern job market, such as coding and financial literacy.

cards.d: A rite is a traditional ceremony carried out by a particular group or society.
cards.e: Special masks are worn during the rite when a new baby is born.
cards.ielts: In many cultures, graduating from university is seen as an important rite of passage into adult life.

cards.d: To stall means to stop a process and continue it at a later time.
cards.e: If you give the car a push, it won’t stall.
cards.ielts: Peace talks between the two countries stalled after neither side was willing to compromise on the border issue.

cards.d: If something is supernatural, it is not real or explainable by natural law.
cards.e: The dragon had supernatural powers such as flying and breathing fire.
cards.ielts: Many popular films and novels feature supernatural creatures, which some parents believe are unsuitable for young children.
